_comment: WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets work
THROUGH. make verify and the CI doc-helper-flags-check step read its green as
'no instruction document passes a helper a flag it lacks', and nothing
downstream re-derives that. A blind version prints the same ok line while a
driver tells a stuck worker to run a command that exits 2 - the #1835 state.
THE CASES ARE MINIATURE TREES (--root): a fixture mailbox helper that accepts
--to/--from/--body, and one template. The BAD pair covers the single-line form
and the backslash-continued form most real invocations take. The GOOD case holds
the shapes a naive extractor gets wrong: flags inside a $(...) substitution, a
flag after a pipe, a .sh wrapper handing off to a .py parser that builds its
option names, and a flag mentioned in prose after an inline span closes.

cases.name: bad-unknown-flag
cases.why: The #1835 shape on one line: an escalation command passing --kind to a mailbox whose parser rejects it. If this scores GOOD the gate cannot see the defect it was written for.

cases.name: bad-continuation-line
cases.why: The same unknown flag on a backslash-continued line. Most multi-line helper invocations in the command documents take this shape; a gate reading one physical line would pass it.

cases.name: bad-flag-after-quoted-separator
cases.why: The unknown flag sits after a quoted argument holding '#' and ';'. The first cut of the gate split at punctuation without reading quotes and passed this; counter-model review found it. If it scores GOOD, any quoted message with a hash or semicolon hides every flag after it.

cases.name: good-known-flags
cases.why: THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate in make verify: every shape the live documents use that a naive extractor misreads - substitution, pipe, delegated parser with computed option names, prose after an inline span. A gate that flags any of them blocks every merge. It also holds a quoted --body whose TEXT contains --kind, '#' and ';': reading quoted text as flags would block a valid command over its message wording.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new. This is the weaker check the obvious framing produces - confirm each named helper exists. It misses both BAD cases, where the helper exists and the flag does not, and agrees with the gate on the GOOD case.
